transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Dana Morris (ScaleLayer CTO); Luis Ortega (ML Eng); Priya Shah (Infra); Jamie Lee (PM)
Meeting link and artifacts: benchmark-spreadsheet.xlsx (shared), redwood-sec-pack.pdf (link), run-logs.tar.gz (pending)

Summary (auto): quick review of last week's runs, deep dive into p50/p95 numbers, discussion about dedicated vs hosted for production KPIs, agree to rerun with 8k/16k contexts and adjusted batching.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, quick agenda, we'll run through the benchmark slides, call out things that look off, then figure out next steps. Dana you still have time right?
[00:12] Dana Morris: yea all good, thanks. We want to focus on the p95s mostly, also curious about high conc concurrency, we saw spikes with the baseline provider last week.
[00:22] Samir Patel: cool, so just to re-iterate config, the Redwood runs used g4dn-like hardware w/ 1 shard per GPU, 4-concurrent batches by default, int8 quant, and prefix KV cache enabled for repeat prefixes — though the transcribe sometimes shows KV as K-V cach.
[00:38] Luis Ortega: small note, our baseline uses BaselineCloud's managed endpoint, single model instance with autoscale turned on, we used their recommended batch size of 2 which is probably why throughput was lower.
[00:50] Jamie Lee: and our SLO is p95 < 350ms for short prompts, and p95 < 800ms for long 8k context prompts, is that how you all are measuring?
[01:03] Samir Patel: yes exact that; slide 3 shows p50/p95 for model small-b and model mid-c across three concurrency levels.
[01:18] Avery Chen: I'll share my screen, slide one — baseline vs Redwood p50: Redwood is ~30-40% faster on p50 across most short prompt cases, p95 is better by ~20% except at high concurrency for model mid-c where baseline spikes lower.
[01:40] Dana Morris: I saw that in the spreadsheet, curious if the baseline's lower p95 at high concurrency is due to their batching strategy or because they throttle long requests differently.
[01:51] Samir Patel: likely batching; BaselineCloud's autoscaler can spin up thin instances under load which helps tail under certain configs, but their per-token cost is much higher so tradeoffs. Our config was conservative for the POC to match their concurrency shape but we might need to tune batch formation window.
[02:10] Luis Ortega: can you explain what you mean by batch formation window? we tried to set max_latency to 20ms but maybe that was too low.
[02:19] Samir Patel: yeah so Redwood's runtime has a batching window that waits up to X ms to form a batch. Setting to a slightly higher window (like 40-60ms) can improve throughput and often reduces p95 for medium-length prompts because GPU utilization improves, though it can increase p50 slightly.
[02:36] Priya Shah: are there safety concerns increasing the batch window? we worry about latency SLOs.
[02:43] Samir Patel: it's a tradeoff; we can do dynamic windows by load class, and we also have KV/prefix caching to avoid re-computing repeated prefixes which helps latency without changing batch window.
[02:56] Jamie Lee: the spreadsheet's run 20260722-run3 has a weird outlier at 95th, is that captured in the logs?
[03:05] Samir Patel: yes that's in the logs, I think that run had a GC pause on the host fragment, the telemetry flagged it as infra noise. We'll surface raw logs with timestamps.
[03:18] Dana Morris: ok good — the 8k context tests, Redwood did well on throughput but p95 was over our 800ms target in one run. Thoughts?
[03:28] Samir Patel: for 8k we were using model-mid-c quantized (int8) with KV cache warmed for repeated prompts. The run that missed p95 had cold KV and also default small batch size; rerunning with warmed cache + a slightly larger batch window brought p95 down close to target. We'll re-run and include a warmed cache scenario.
[03:48] Luis Ortega: on the baseline side they do a two-tier routing where long-context requests go to a different fleet. That explains some tail differences. Can Redwood emulate that routing?
[03:59] Avery Chen: yes we can set routing policies to isolate long-context work to dedicated nodes or dedicated capacity; that's what Dedicated was built for. It also makes billing predictable.
[04:10] Dana Morris: how much lift to try Dedicated for 30 days? We want a smoke test to compare apples-to-apples with BaselineCloud dedicated-ish fleet.
[04:19] Avery Chen: we can do a 30-day trial with a small dedicated pool, Samir can help size. I'll send pricing and a draft SOW.
[04:26] Jamie Lee: security ask — we need SOC2 and a data residency note for EU logs. Do you have that?
[04:33] Samir Patel: yes we have SOC2 and can provide redacted audit logs; I'll share the security pack link. Note: for private/EU residency we can deploy a private control plane with customer managed KMS.
[04:49] Priya Shah: perfect. Last week baseline gave us token cost numbers, can Redwood share per-token cost assumptions used in the spreadsheet?
[04:58] Avery Chen: yes included a cost tab, but I'll send a clearer breakdown — e.g., per-1k token cost with int8, plus amortized dedicated GPU price for the trial.
[05:08] Samir Patel: moving on, slide 4 shows concurrency sweeps — at 16 concurrent sessions Redwood's throughput is about 1.4x baseline for model-small-b, but for model-mid-c at high concurrency baseline was slightly better on p95.
[05:24] Luis Ortega: that was surprising, any reason?
[05:28] Samir Patel: short answer: kernel selection and per-request overhead. For mid-c the baseline's newer kernel path produced slightly lower tail under our default small batch. When we increased batch formation window and enabled fused attention kernels in our runtime (experimental flag), p95 improved. There's an experimental tuning flag in our runtime that picks a different attention kernel depending on sequence length distribution.
[05:50] Dana Morris: is that flag production-ready?
[05:53] Samir Patel: it's marked as stable for dedicated customers; for hosted it rolls out conservatively. We can enable it for your POC dedicated pool. There's a tiny risk of increased memory, but we'll monitor.
[06:08] Jamie Lee: any quantization regressions we should watch for? We saw some small quality diffs when moving from fp16 to int8.
[06:16] Samir Patel: yes int8 can introduce slight probability mass shifts. For customer-sensitive prompts we recommend running eval sets; Redwood Optimize can suggest per-layer quantization settings or keep critical layers in fp16. We ran a sample eval and saw quality delta <1.5% on our metric.
[06:33] Priya Shah: timeline — if you rerun by next Monday and we validate, how quickly can dedicated be stood up?
[06:40] Avery Chen: we can provision a dedicated pool in 2-3 business days after purchase, longer for private on-prem provisioning.
[06:47] Dana Morris: ok that's fine.
[06:50] Samir Patel: back to numbers — I'll call out a few specific rows in the spreadsheet: model-small-b short-prompt p95 baseline 420ms Redwood 310ms; model-mid-c long-context p95 baseline 760ms Redwood 820ms (but improved to 700ms with larger batch window / warmed cache).
[07:12] Jamie Lee: can you include exact run ids in the sheet? makes it easier to correlate.
[07:17] Samir Patel: yes we'll add run ids and commit hashes for the runtime.
[07:24] Luis Ortega: what about the KV cache warm-up time? how many requests to warm?
[07:30] Samir Patel: depends on prompt diversity, but typically 2-3 repeated prefixes warms the hot paths; we can also pre-populate cache for known patterns.
[07:41] Dana Morris: we have a lot of repeated system prompts so that should help.
[07:46] Priya Shah: network egress — BaselineCloud included egress in their cost model, how is Redwood measured?
[07:53] Avery Chen: hosted API includes egress; dedicated trial billing can be structured either with egress included or passed through. We'll outline options in pricing.
[08:03] Jamie Lee: any red flags from Redwood side for our test harness? we run 500rps for 10m windows.
[08:10] Samir Patel: 500rps sustained is fine for Dedicated, for hosted it depends on quota; for POC we can support a sustained burst if we coordinate. We did a 10m window test in run 20260722-run2 which looked stable.
[08:23] Dana Morris: ok good.
[08:26] Avery Chen: action items recap — Samir will rerun 8k/16k with warmed cache and larger batch windows, Priya to provide VPC creds to mirror baseline networking, Avery to send pricing and SOC2 docs.
[08:40] Jamie Lee: who owns the follow-up call scheduling?
[08:43] Avery Chen: I'll schedule next sync for Monday 2026-08-03 after the rerun results come in.
[08:50] Luis Ortega: quick question — you mentioned an experimental fused attention kernel, is that the same as the fused-attn that was in your docs? we had earlier seen a doc reference as "fuse-att" which confuses folks.
[09:02] Samir Patel: yes that's likely the doc mismatch, our docs had a typo; we'll correct it and point to the exact runtime flag.
[09:10] Dana Morris: ok great. Anything else on security/compliance?
[09:14] Priya Shah: just confirm KMS options for dedicated trial — customer-managed KMS is a hard requirement for production.
[09:21] Avery Chen: agreed, for production we support customer KMS; for POC we can do redacted keys but will plan for KMS integration if you move to Dedicated.
[09:31] Jamie Lee: last item, can Redwood run an apples-to-apples cost calc if we give you BaselineCloud invoice samples?
[09:36] Avery Chen: yes send invoices, we'll produce a cost comparison including amortized GPU and per-token cost assumptions.
[09:42] Samir Patel: ok that's it from our side.
[09:45] Dana Morris: thanks everyone, appreciate the detail — excited to see rerun results.
[09:50] Avery Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links by end of week.

End of transcript.

Artifacts referenced: benchmark-spreadsheet.xlsx (sheet: latency_vs_baseline), redwood-sec-pack.pdf (link: https://redwood.example.com/sec-pack), run logs (S3 link to be shared), pricing draft (doc link pending).
